purpose: Cefuroxime is an antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections, including ear infections, sinus infections, bronchitis, urinary tract infections, skin infections, and Lyme disease. It works against many common bacteria that cause infections in everyday life. It is only effective against bacterial infections and will not work for viral illnesses like the cold or flu.
how_it_works: Cefuroxime works by attacking the outer wall that surrounds bacteria. Think of the bacterial wall like a protective shell — cefuroxime blocks the bacteria from building and maintaining that shell. Without a strong wall, the bacteria fall apart and die, clearing the infection from your body.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, stomach upset, and vomiting. Some people may notice a headache or dizziness. Taking the tablet form with food can help reduce stomach discomfort. A mild skin rash can also occasionally occur.
warnings: Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to penicillin antibiotics, as there is a small chance of a similar allergic reaction to cefuroxime. Stop taking it and seek help right away if you develop hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of your face or throat. Let your healthcare team know if you have kidney problems, as your dose may need adjusting. Taking antibiotics can sometimes cause a severe type of diarrhea — if your diarrhea becomes persistent, bloody, or severe, contact your doctor right away. Always finish the full course even if you feel better early.
typical_dosing: For most adults, the typical dose is 250 mg to 500 mg taken by mouth twice a day, usually for 5 to 10 days depending on the infection. Tablets should be taken with food to improve absorption and reduce stomach upset. Children's doses are based on their weight and are usually given as a liquid suspension. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your situation.
